name: The Pacific War: From Manchuria to the Bomb
description: Japan's war in Asia and the Pacific, from the seizure of Manchuria and the war in China through Pearl Harbor, Midway and the island battles to the atomic bombs and surrender.

checkpoints.name: Empire and the war in China
checkpoints.note: The Empire of Japan grows strong after 1868, beats China in 1895, rules Korea from 1910 and in 1932 sets up Manchukuo in Manchuria under Hirohito's reign. From 1937 the Second Sino-Japanese War sets Japan against Chiang Kai-shek's Republic of China, with Mao's communists fighting too, and the Nanjing Massacre follows the fall of the capital.

checkpoints.name: Pearl Harbor to Midway
checkpoints.note: Tojo's government goes to war in December 1941. Yamamoto's carriers strike Pearl Harbor and Japan sweeps south, taking Hong Kong, Singapore and the oil of the Dutch East Indies. Six months later Nimitz's carriers sink four Japanese carriers at Midway.

checkpoints.name: Island by island
checkpoints.note: From Guadalcanal, Allied forces under Nimitz and MacArthur advance across the Pacific. MacArthur returns to the Philippines, and the Battle of Leyte Gulf in 1944 destroys much of what is left of Japan's navy. In China the war grinds on, and the new B-29 bombers come within reach of Japan's cities.

checkpoints.name: The bomb and surrender
checkpoints.note: Iwo Jima falls in March 1945, the giant battleship Yamato is sunk in April on its way to Okinawa, and Aung San turns Burma's army against Japan. Atomic bombs fall on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August and Hirohito accepts surrender. The Tokyo trials judge the wartime leaders, and a new constitution in 1947 founds the post-war state of Japan.
